recipes.name: Baked Penne and Smoked Sausage
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package Hillshire Farm® Smoked Sausage
1 (10.75 ounce) can cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Cut sausage into 1/4-inch slices.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Add sausage; cook and stir for 3 to 4 minutes or until lightly browned.
Combine soup and milk in a 13x9-inch baking dish. Stir in uncooked pasta, sausage, 1/2 cup French-fried onions, 1/2 cup cheese and peas. Cover baking dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 45 minutes. Remove foil and top with remaining 1 cup French-fried onions and 1/2 cup cheese. Bake for 3 minutes or until cheese is melted. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Penne and Smoked Sausage
raw_recipe.description: Hillshire Farm® Smoked Sausage is baked in a creamy sauce with pasta, French-fried onions, cheese, and peas in this easy one-dish meal.

review.reviewBody: First I must say I am reviewing the original recipe that appeared in magazine advertisements several years ago. I don't know why they changed the recipe because the original one was great. The differences are...use cream of celery soup instead of the mushroom soup, use 1 1/2 cups milk instead of 2 1/2, use 4 cups cooked penne, which is 2 1/2 cups uncooked or 8 oz., use mozzarella instead of cheddar and use the cheddar French Fried Onions. Put together the same way but bake uncovered for 30 minutes before adding remaining onions and cheese and baking the additional 3 minutes. I did make 2 variations from this recipe, I used 2 cups fully cooked cubed ham instead of the sausage only because my husband doesn't like sausage, and I used half mozzarella and half cheddar. This turned out great and was loved by everyone. The changes I made weren't enough to affect my rating because this would be excellent as written (magazine version). Give it a try.

So delicious and easy. I only used two cups of milk. I used frozen kale since it was the only frozen veggie I had on hand. I also used mozzarella cheese in the mixture and an Italian mix of cheese for the top. I also used breadcrumbs on the top and did not used fried onions (just didn’t have them on hand). I did put sautéed onions in the mixture just because my family loves onion. The whole family (even my young kids) gobbled this right up. I will definitely keep this recipe.

I have made this recipe twice. Once exactly as directed and tonight with quite a few modifications. The first time I enjoyed it but the second time it was much better. First I par-cooked the whole wheat penne noodles to insure thorough cooking and less oven time. Secondly, I browned the sausage (turkey) with some onion, garlic and red bell pepper (left over that needed to be used up). Third, I combined the reduced fat cream of mushroom, 1.5 C skim milk and 1 C reduced fat colby jack (all I had) along with a dash of cayenne pepper and heated it on the stove until the cheese had melted. Finally I combined everything, along with 1/2 C peas and 1/2 C corn (left over, as well). I covered everything with another sprinkling of cheese and covered with foil, baking for 20 min. After 20 minutes, I removed the foil and topped with some herbed buttered bread crumbs combined with a few tablespoons of Parmesan cheese, which I sprinkled over the top (I didn't have any French Fried Onions). This was very good. Thanks for the great recipe. It's simple and easy and though not terribly healthful, it's excellent comfort food. The modifications I've made, though more work, made for faster cook time and allowed everything to blend better.

I followed this recipe about 80% of the way and it turned out fabulous! Here's what I did: I used 6 spinach and asiago flavored chicken sausages cut up and sauted until browned with 1.5 diced green pepper and about 1c of diced onion, sauted all in olive oil until onions were tender. I par-boiled the noodles because I hate the way uncooked noodles come out in casseroles. Drained pasta and added it to sausage mixture, as well as two cans of cream of mushroom soup and about 1.5c milk. Mixed everything together and poured into a large casserole dish, topped with cheddar flavored French-fried onions, and sprinkled a mixture of cheddar, mozz., and colby cheeses on top. Baked at 350 for about 30 mins until the top was lightly browned. I made a large glass casserole dish full of this. This was fantastic and both my bf and I went back for more.

pretty good casserole. I went with some suggestions from a reviewer who talked about the "original recipe" Used cream of celery instead of mushroom. I precooked the noodles, decreased the milk to 1 1/2 cups and added chedder cheese along with some onion powder and seasoning salt to milk soup combo. Baked 350 for 20 min, then topped with the fried onions and colby jack cheese/mozz cheese.

I made this last night for me and my boyfriend, and we both loved it! He is a super picky eater, but he said it's a re-do dinner for sure. I added a bit more pasta than it called for because it just looked too soupy. I also added more french fried onions as well. Turned out perfect. At first I thought it was going to be a bust because after 45 minutes it was soupy and the pasta wasn't done. I cooked it for 10 more minutes, and then took the foil off, added more cheese and onions and let bake for about 5 more minutes. I let it sit for about 7 minutes, and it thickened up quick, and the pasta was perfect.

This has been one of my go to meals every month since I discovered it in 2009. Just for reference, add 1/2 cup more milk than advertised, that ensures less burnt to a crisp pasta. Also, add 10-15 minutes more to cooking time if you are not using the recommended size baking dish.

This was an awesome recipe! I did change a few things however! Instead of using pasta I substituted potatoes in! I added salt and pepper and cooked it a longer just to make sure the potatoes got done. It's delicious and creamy! I will be making this again! :)

This was better than I expected. (I'm always wary of easy recipes). I omitted the cheese (I don't NEED it) and only used about 1/4 or so of the pasta. I sub mixed vegs for the peas and only had about 3/4 cup fried onions, which I stirred all into the dish. It turned out nice and saucy. I may add a bit more veggies next time.

This is a very tasty and easy recipe. I deducted a star because of calories content. I added broccoli and substituted sausage with ham. I suggest mixing the cream sauce ingredients over the stove top (soup, milk and cheese) before cooking it in the oven. This allows for a more even and creamier texture and also speeds the cooking process along.

This was good and yes, the kids liked it (a huge plus) After reading other reviews I decided to use turkey sausage; I also partially cooked the noodles, used cream of celery soup, and added 1 1/2c milk instead of 2 1/2. The only alteration I made on my own was that, instead of ff onions, I used crushed potato chips (and no cheese on top-- didn't need it) Honestly, I think you could easily omit the fattening toppers altogether and still have a mild, tasty, and kid-friendly comfort meal. I'll make it again
For those who are getting raw pasta you need to make sure your baking pan is tightly covered if the steam escapes the pasta won't cook properly

the liquid ran over the pan in the oven, even with it covered with foil. made a mess in the oven, set the smoke alarm off too.. other than that it was good, it was done ahead of time. I would add a little less milk or just do the whole thing in a skillet next time.

I love this dish and love to make it for friends and family and is always a hit! My 8 year old even loves it! I have been making it for over 10 years and always keep the ingredients on hand to make. This is great leftover, just add a splash of mik before heating and she fresh fried onions. The original fried onions will work too, but the flavor of the cheddar fried onions really brings out all the flavors. Don't pass on this recipe, making this tonight!
The recipe was delicious as written, no changes are needed.

Good recipe. Followed reciepe as written except i added a cup of sliced carrots. Had to add 30 minutes to the covered cook time
to get pasta tender. Also used four pepper smoked sausage which gave it a little spice. Will make again.
my pasta came out Raw. I double the recipe because I have 4 boys and we ended up ordering pizza. added 30 more minutes and still pasta was raw.
This is terrible! Followed recipe to a T and it came out w in th most of the pasta still uncooked! Never thickened up at all. It was very runny and quite off putting!
Everyone loved it. Yes, I will make it again.

Delicious! I made it as the recipe is written, only adding a can of mushrooms to the mix. Everything came out perfect! I had no issues with excess liquid or uncooked pasta, and it tasted fantastic. This one is going into rotation for sure!
